messages.subject: Re: org.renjin.eval.EvalException: object 'C_logit_link' not found
messages.body_plain:
This references C code from the stats package that is not yet included in renjin's build. You can try copying the relevant source from  http://svn.r-project.org/R/tags/R-2-14-2/src/library/stats/src/loglin.c

to packages/stats/src/main/c

though you may also have to tinker with gcc-bridge to get it compiling.

Otherwise filing a bug report with the attached code would be very helpful!

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: renjin with java matrix data set
messages.subject_clean: renjin with java matrix data set
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ragnar,

A "matrix" in R is simply a vector with a dimension ("dim") attribute. The R syntax for accessing matrix elements is Matrix[1,2].

To create a matrix from Java code, you can use the DoubleMatrixBuilder utility class:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/renjin/primitives/matrix/DoubleMatrixBuilder.java

This will create an R matrix in memory with the appropriate dimension attribute.

You can also subclass the DoubleVector class if your matrix is strangely shaped or not stored in memory.

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: renjin with java matrix data set
messages.subject_clean: renjin with java matrix data set
messages.body_plain:
Column and row names for R matrices are specified in the "dimnames" attribute, which should be a ListVector containing a StringVector each dimension. In R, this looks like:

x <- c(1,2,3,4,5,6)
attr(x, "dim") <- c(2L, 3L) # now a 2 x 3 matrix
attr(x, "dimnames") <- list( c("row 1", "row 2"), c("column 1", "column 2", "column 3") )

This will then look like this in R:
> x
      column 1 column 2 column 3
row 1        1        3        5
row 2        2        4        6

You can construct the dimnames attribute in Java using the ListVector.Builder and the StringArrayVector.Builder classes (or StringArrayVector.valueOf("row 1", "row 2") if the names are fixed)

A data.frame object in R is something else. It's basically a list of columns. In R, you could construct one by "hand" in the following way

> df <- list( c(1,2,3,4), c(10,20,30,40 ))   # Create a list of two columns
> attr(df, "names") <- c("x", "y")   # Give those columns names
> attr(df, "row.names") <- as.character(1:4) # Assign row names
> attr(df, "class") <- "data.frame"
> df
  x  y
1 1 10
2 2 20
3 3 30
4 4 40

Note again that your data doesn't have to sit in memory, you can provide your own implementation of IntVector or StringVector for your own data sources.

What we really need is a good little library of helper functions for Java developers that would facilitate the creation of all these different types of R objects: data.frames, matrices, time series, etc, because it can be definitely a little opaque.

HTH
Alex

messages.subject: Re: Renjin and forecast package.
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

It looks like the forecast package "Depends" on colorspace, so it will fail when loading unfortunately.

The java methods that you're looking at are just the C/Fortran components of the forecast package and will likely not be much use. The R code is serialized in AST form as a resource, and is evaluated at runtime.

Unfortunatley time for Renjin has a bit short in December due to other projects, but I think that the next release should solve this problem. If you don't mind getting your hands dirty in the meantime, I can suggest checking out Renjin from master, and setting up a maven build for the forecast package in the same format that you see the stats package in Renjin's repo (https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/tree/master/packages/stats) and remove the bits that depend on colorspace.

More time for Renjin and the next release is coming in the new year!

Best,
Alex

messages.subject: Re: resource org/renjin/stats/environment not found?
messages.body_plain:
There's been a change to the way packages are serialized, (large objects are now stored seperately) it's meant to be backwards with the previous impl, but perhaps something went wrong with the merge?

See https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/9a53834c266fbeaf71a19861562c921dbbbd52b8

Hth,
Alex
